title: MCV2 immunization, SDG regions compared
headline: Central and Southern Asia: MCV2 coverage up 83 points since 2004
subtitle: Percentage of children who received the 2nd dose of measles-containing vaccine, as per administered in the national schedule
years: Central and S. Asia: from 6% in 2004 to 89% in 2024. World: from 22% to 76%.
data_line: Data: WHO/UNICEF WUENIC via UN SDG Global Database, series SH_ACS_MCV2, extracted 1 Nov 2026
alt: Central and Southern Asia: MCV2 coverage up 83 points since 2004. Central and S. Asia: from 6% in 2004 to 89% in 2024. World: from 22% to 76%. Sub-Saharan Africa: 2% in 2004 to 54% in 2024; N. Africa and W. Asia: 67% in 2004 to 78% in 2024; Central and S. Asia: 6% in 2004 to 89% in 2024; E. and S.-E. Asia: 10% in 2004 to 88% in 2024; Latin America, Caribbean: 56% in 2004 to 69% in 2024; Oceania (excl. Aus., NZ): 4% in 2004 to 34% in 2024; Australia and NZ: 70% in 2004 to 91% in 2024; Europe and N. America: 73% in 2004 to 90% in 2024; World: 22% in 2004 to 76% in 2024
question: What lies behind the change in MCV2 coverage in Central and Southern Asia, and what could others learn from it?
